title: Embed scale semantics and swappable metric runtime with opt-in legacy compatibility
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem: Clients and internal components have ambiguous expectations about whether embedding vectors returned by models are L2-normalized and whether similarity should be computed with cosine or raw dot product. This ambiguity causes: inconsistent reranking scores across model variants, subtle production regressions when swapping quantized or distilled models, and correctness bugs for customers that compare scores across embeddings from different sources.

Goal: Implement an explicit, runtime-level mechanism to control and declare embedding scale semantics per-request and ensure backward-compatible behavior for existing customers. Deliver both a low-latency path for non-normalized dot workloads and a normalization-on-read option with measured cost, plus a compatibility shim so legacy clients keep existing scores until they opt into the new semantics.
acceptance_criteria: API: Support a request header or parameter 'embed_metric' with values 'dot' | 'cosine' | 'auto'. 'auto' preserves current default behavior for legacy clients.

Runtime: Implement two optimized code paths: a low-latency dot-path that avoids per-request L2 normalization, and a normalization path that applies fast vector normalization using SSE/AVX/GPU kernels depending on hardware.
Backward compatibility: Default behavior remains identical to current product for existing clients unless they explicitly specify 'embed_metric'.
Tests: Unit and integration tests validate numerical parity with reference numpy implementations for both metrics across representative models (float32, fp16, int8-quantized).
Performance: Normalization path adds no more than 8% tail latency at 99th percentile for 1-4k vector workloads; dot-path latency must be within 2% of current baseline for common batch sizes.
Telemetry: Emit a new metric 'embed.metric.selected' with tags for 'dot'|'cosine'|'auto' and a histogram for added normalization CPU/GPU time.
Migration: Documented migration guide for customers explaining when to choose cosine vs dot and an example showing how to opt in and validate score parity.
technical_notes: Design: Add a lightweight header 'X-Embed-Metric' accepted by REST and SDKs; SDKs should expose an enum to avoid typos.

Implementation: At serving runtime entry, branch on metric: if dot -> compute dot product directly; if cosine -> normalize left and right vectors before dot. For batched requests, normalization should be fused with the existing per-batch packing to reduce memory copies.

KV cache/Prefix caching: Normalizing on read cannot change cached prefix scores but normalization must be applied deterministically when computing similarity for re-ranking. Ensure cache keys include model variant and 'embed_metric' when the cache stores precomputed similarities.
Quantized models: When using int8 kernels, apply normalization in float compute to avoid quantization instability. Add fast path for fp16 fused normalization on GPU.
API compatibility: 'auto' maps to current default historically (dot for older clients); servers will log deprecation warnings before changing default mapping in a future release.

Metrics/Observability: Track fraction of requests using each metric, normalization cost breakdown, and customer-impacting regressions by correlating metric selection with rerank quality metrics from evaluations.
Edge cases: Zero vectors should return similarity 0 for cosine and dot to match historical semantics; implement robust epsilon handling to avoid NaNs.
migration_steps: 1) Implement header and runtime branch behind a feature flag 'embed_metric_runtime' and deploy to canary hosts.
2) Roll out SDK changes to set header when users opt in (patch release) and include examples in the changelog.
3) Enable telemetry and gather dataset of production uses and any quality regressions for 4 weeks.
4) Provide a customer-facing guide and a small evaluation harness (notebook + sample prompts) to validate score behavior across models.
5) After validation, remove feature flag and set default mapping of 'auto' -> 'dot' for backward compat, still allowing explicit 'cosine' opt-ins.
6) After 90 days and customer communication, consider toggling default if community feedback warrants making 'cosine' the default for new clients.
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of requests on a small set of clusters with feature flag on (2 weeks)
Staged: 25% -> 60% over two additional weeks while monitoring metrics
Global: Remove flag and enable on all hosts once latency and correctness thresholds met
SDK: Release patches to JS/Python/Go with opt-in API and examples the day of canary start
test_plan: Unit tests for numeric parity (numpy reference) covering fp32, fp16, int8 quantized vectors
Microbenchmarks for per-request latency with synthetic batches of sizes [1,4,16,64] and vector dims [512,1024,2048].
Integration tests: end-to-end reranker flow that compares ranking order across metric choices for known datasets (MS MARCO subset, internal query pairs).
Canary monitoring: synthetic traffic with golden expected rerank outputs to detect regressions within 5 minutes of deploy.
Chaos: brief pod restarts during canary to ensure stable fallback and no stateful assumptions about normalization state.
risks: Latency regressions for normalization path on CPU-heavy clusters causing customer-visible SLO violations.
Subtle score drift across models leading to re-ranking A/B regressions — must be validated per-model.
Cache fragmentation if cache keys include metric, increasing memory pressure; mitigate with TTL and eviction policy adjustments.
Customer confusion: making cosine the default without clear communication may break downstream scoring thresholds.
Implementation bugs in quantized normalization can introduce numerical instability; requires careful unit testing.
